question: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which AB || DC, and E and F are the mid points of the diagonals AC and BD, respectively. If AB = 45 cm, BC = 96 cm, DC = 53 cm, and AD = 37 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of EF?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The distance between the midpoints of the diagonals of a trapezium is always equal to half the difference of its parallel sides.

Given parallel sides: AB = 45 cm and DC = 53 cm.

Length of EF = 1/2 × (DC − AB)

Length of EF = 1/2 × (53 − 45) = 1/2 × 8 = 4 cm.

*(Note: The lengths of the non-parallel sides AD and BC are given only to distract and are not needed.)*

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a trapezium with AB || DC.

Length of the parallel side AB = 45 cm.

Length of the parallel side DC = 53 cm.

E and F are the midpoints of the diagonals AC and BD respectively.

**Formula Used:**

If a line segment connects the midpoints of the diagonals of a trapezium, it is parallel to the parallel sides, and its length is equal to half the difference of their lengths.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Length of EF = 1/2 × (DC − AB)

⇒ EF = 1/2 × (53 − 45)

⇒ EF = 1/2 × 8

⇒ EF = 4 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mid-segment of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides of a trapezium is parallel to its bases. Its length is half the sum of the parallel sides. Length = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Area of a Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is calculated as half the product of the sum of its parallel sides and the perpendicular height between them. Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Isosceles Trapezium Properties

If the non-parallel sides of a trapezium are equal in length, it is called an isosceles trapezium. Its diagonals are of equal length, and the angles at the base are identical.
